preamble.title: cardano-foundation/cip113-programmable-tokens
preamble.description: Aiken implementation of CIP-113 programmable tokens

cardano/address/Credential.title: Credential
cardano/address/Credential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/transaction/OutputReference.title: OutputReference
cardano/transaction/OutputReference.description:
An `OutputReference` is a unique reference to an output on-chain. The `output_index`
 corresponds to the position in the output list of the transaction (identified by its id)
 that produced that output

registry_node/RegistryNode.title: RegistryNode
registry_node/RegistryNode.description:
Registry node in the linked list of registered programmable token policies
 This represents an entry in the CIP-113 registry.

 Field order is load-bearing: it determines the CBOR layout consumed by both
 on-chain and off-chain code. The three script-credential fields are ordered
 by the natural lifecycle of a programmable token — `minting_logic_script`
 (mint), `transfer_logic_script` (transfer), `third_party_transfer_logic_script`
 (admin) — with `minting_logic_script` first because registration is the
 earliest event in a token's lifetime.

fields.title: key
fields.description: The key (currency symbol) of the programmable token policy

fields.title: next
fields.description: The next key in lexicographical order (for linked list traversal)

fields.title: minting_logic_script
fields.description:
The minting logic script credential. The substandard's withdraw-0 minting
 logic finds its own registry node by equality on this field — that gives
 it the `key` (the policy id) without recomputing the issuance hash.
 `registry_mint` also cryptographically binds this field to the policy id
 via `is_programmable_token_id_valid`, so the field cannot lie.

fields.title: transfer_logic_script
fields.description: The transfer logic script credential that validates token transfers

fields.title: third_party_transfer_logic_script
fields.description: The third party transfer logic script credential that handles admin actions (seizure, etc.)

fields.title: global_state_cs
fields.description: Optional global state NFT currency symbol for this policy

types/MintingRegistryProof.title: MintingRegistryProof
types/MintingRegistryProof.description:
Redeemer for the issuance minting policy.

 The redeemer is the registry proof itself — a `RefInput` index for a
 subsequent mint (registry node already exists), or an `OutputIndex` for
 the first mint (registry node being created in the same tx).

 The substandard's withdraw-0 invocation (proof of instance) is checked
 directly against the validator's `minting_logic_cred` parameter — no
 separate redeemer field needed. The validator parameter is baked into
 the policy id at compile time and pinned to `registry.minting_logic_script`
 by the cryptographic binding in `registry_mint`, so collision-resistance
 of blake2b_224 forces credential agreement without a runtime equality
 check on the redeemer.

types/ProgrammableLogicGlobalRedeemer.title: ProgrammableLogicGlobalRedeemer
types/ProgrammableLogicGlobalRedeemer.description: Redeemer for the global programmable logic stake validator

anyOf.title: TransferAct
anyOf.description: Transfer action with proofs for each token type

anyOf.title: ThirdPartyAct
anyOf.description:
Third party action for administrative / compliance operations —
 forced transfer, seizure, freeze enforcement, or burn. Supports multiple
 UTxOs of the subject policy in a single transaction.

fields.title: registry_node_idx
fields.description: Index of the registry node in reference inputs

fields.title: outputs_start_idx
fields.description: Starting index in outputs where processed outputs begin

anyOf.title: UnfrackingAct
anyOf.description:
Finding 17: Unfracking action — let a holder redistribute the
 programmable tokens they already hold across multiple PLB UTxOs
 WITHOUT invoking any substandard transfer logic. Used to break
 up multi-policy UTxOs into single-policy UTxOs so a freeze on
 one policy stops collateral-damaging unrelated policies that
 happened to share the same UTxO.

 No payload: the unfracking validator infers everything it needs
 from the transaction shape. Caller proves authorisation by
 signing for (or invoking the script of) every PLB input being
 unfracked; the validator enforces value conservation per policy
 at the PLB boundary and refuses to route tokens to any stake
 credential the caller did not authorise.

 The invariants do NOT live in programmable_logic_global: under
 this redeemer, PLG only requires that the standalone
 `unfracking` withdraw-0 validator (whose credential is the
 `unfracking_cred` field of the protocol-params datum) is invoked
 in the same transaction. This keeps the hot-path PLG reference
 script ~600 bytes smaller; only unfracking transactions pay for
 the unfracking logic.

types/RegistryProof.title: RegistryProof
types/RegistryProof.description: Proof that a token is (or is not) in the registry

anyOf.title: TokenExists
anyOf.description: Token exists in the registry at this reference input index

anyOf.title: TokenDoesNotExist
anyOf.description: Token does not exist (proof via covering node at this index)

types/RegistryRedeemer.title: RegistryRedeemer
types/RegistryRedeemer.description: Redeemer for registry minting policy (linked list operations)

anyOf.title: RegistryInit
anyOf.description: Initialize the registry with the origin node

anyOf.title: RegistryInsert
anyOf.description:
Insert a new programmable token policy into the registry.

 `minting_logic_script` is the credential of the substandard's
 withdraw-0 minting logic. registry_mint enforces that:
   * the new node's datum field `minting_logic_script` equals this
     value (datum-matches-redeemer check, prevents the registrar
     from writing a different credential into the datum than they
     claim in the redeemer);
   * the issuance template parameterised with this credential hashes
     to `key` (cryptographic binding: the `hashed_param` used in the
     policy id derivation is the inner 28-byte hash of this
     credential — derived inside the validator, NOT supplied as a
     separate redeemer field);
   * the substandard's withdraw-0 logic is invoked
     (`minting_logic_script` in `tx.withdrawals`).

 Whether the registration also carries a first mint of the new
 policy is NOT constrained by registry_mint: a first mint in the
 same tx is validated by `issuance_mint` as usual, and registering
 without any mint is equally valid (useful for real-world-asset
 issuance or supply-aware substandards that must initialise global
 state before any token exists). A substandard that wants a strict
 register-then-mint lifecycle must enforce it in its own minting
 logic.
